title: A denser fluid pushes back
hook: Change fluid density and predict buoyant force.
misconception: buoyant force stays fixed when fluid density doubles.
objective: Apply F_b = ρgV to compare buoyant force when fluid density changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed submerged volume under fixed gravity, F_b = ρgV. When fluid density doubles, buoyant force becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F_b = ρgV; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed submerged volume under fixed gravity, with a nonzero initial result. If fluid density triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on buoyant force?
recall.why: Apply F_b = ρgV under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
